title: Long-acting injectable cabotegravir versus daily oral TDF/FTC for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis
topic_state: POOLED -- risk ratio, k=2, direction consistent, magnitude not established
provenance: REGISTRY THROUGHOUT. Every count and denominator is read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results. No publication figure is used.
verification_basis: Both registrations read on 2026-08-18: conditions, arm groups with types, registered primaries, posted results counts.

pooled_hartung_knapp.why_it_is_shown: Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.5 recommends Hartung-Knapp where k is small. Shown ALONGSIDE, not instead. A floor of 1 on the inflation factor means it can never narrow the interval below the unadjusted one.

heterogeneity.how_to_read_this_at_k2: At k=2 these statistics are WEAK evidence about consistency in either direction. Two points cannot demonstrate agreement.
heterogeneity.tau2_estimator: REML -- copied from this block's declared `estimator`, which is the authoritative record of how the pool was computed. NOT inferred: an object that declared no estimator would be left undeclared here, because the absence is itself the finding.
heterogeneity.i2_definition: Higgins I-squared = (Q - df) / Q, clamped at 0. Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.2.
heterogeneity.i2_definition_evidence: Decided by recomputing BOTH definitions from this object's own per-trial inputs: Higgins gives 68.8289 and REML/metafor gives 68.8287 against the stored 68.8000.

per_trial.label: HPTN 083
per_trial.population_as_registered: men who have sex with men and transgender women who have sex with men
per_trial.how: RR = (e1/n1)/(e2/n2); SE(log RR) = sqrt(1/e1 - 1/n1 + 1/e2 - 1/n2), Handbook 6.5 section 6.4.1. Counts read from the registry; the arithmetic is ours and the formula is shown.

per_trial.label: HPTN 084
per_trial.how: RR = (e1/n1)/(e2/n2); SE(log RR) = sqrt(1/e1 - 1/n1 + 1/e2 - 1/n2), Handbook 6.5 section 6.4.1. Counts read from the registry; the arithmetic is ours and the formula is shown.

primary.the_population_difference_stated_on_the_: THE TWO TRIALS ENROL DIFFERENT PEOPLE AND A READER SHOULD SEE THAT BEFORE THE POOLED NUMBER. HPTN 083 enrols men who have sex with men and transgender women; HPTN 084 enrols women. The intervention, the comparator and the registered primary outcome are identical, and the question -- does long-acting injectable cabotegravir prevent HIV infection better than daily oral TDF/FTC -- is the same question in both. THE POOL IS PRESENTED AS AN HIV PRE-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS QUESTION, which is what the title asks, AND NOT as evidence that the effect is the same in both populations. Mode of acquisition and adherence patterns differ between these groups, and k=2 cannot test whether the effect does.

published_synthesis_comparison.status: NOT DONE -- recorded as owed rather than claimed
published_synthesis_comparison.what_is_owed: No published synthesis or regulatory review pooling HPTN 083 and 084 has been searched for or read. Until it is, this estimate has not been checked against anyone else's.

primary.what_this_does_not_establish: NOT that either trial is free of bias -- NO RISK-OF-BIAS ASSESSMENT IS RECORDED. NOT that the effect is equal in men and in women; see the population note above. NOT anything about adherence, which is the mechanism most likely to drive a difference between an injectable and a daily oral regimen and is not an outcome in this pool. NOT reliability of the interval at k=2 -- see Hartung-Knapp.

handbook_authority.handbook: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions
handbook_authority.c62: 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

primary.HETEROGENEITY_AND_HOW_IT_DIFFERS_FROM_TH: I-squared is 68.8% and tau-squared 0.418, which is substantial -- BUT IT IS HETEROGENEITY OF MAGNITUDE, NOT OF DIRECTION, and the distinction changes what may be said. HPTN 083 gives RR 0.33 (0.18-0.62) and HPTN 084 gives RR 0.11 (0.04-0.31). BOTH INTERVALS EXCLUDE 1 AND BOTH FAVOUR CABOTEGRAVIR; the trials disagree about HOW MUCH, not about WHETHER. Contrast the gepotidacin topic built the same day, where one trial excluded 1 and the other did not -- there the pooled point genuinely could not be read as an answer. HERE THE DIRECTION IS CONSISTENT AND THE MAGNITUDE IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The pooled RR 0.21 should be read as: both trials found substantially fewer infections on cabotegravir, and these two trials do not pin down the size of that difference.
primary.the_likely_source_of_the_magnitude_diffe: The two trials enrol different populations with different modes of HIV acquisition and, plausibly, different adherence to a DAILY ORAL comparator -- which is the arm whose performance determines the ratio. That is a HYPOTHESIS. It has NOT been checked against the registrations or any publication, and it is recorded as a hypothesis so that it is not mistaken later for a finding.

house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.estimator: REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.THE_POINT_ESTIMATE_IS_UNCHANGED: The published point is 0.2081 and the house-rule point is 0.2081. THE NUMBER A READER REMEMBERS DOES NOT MOVE; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.variance_inflation_floor: A FLOOR OF 1 IS APPLIED TO THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR so the adjustment can never NARROW an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a KNOWN problem with KNOWN handling rather than a novel judgement.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.no_rule_is_decided_here: The house rule is REML with Hartung-Knapp below k=10, settled days ago. Whether it means ALWAYS or WITH A FLOOR AT k=3 is a decision about this corpus, not a computation, and it has been referred rather than taken. BOTH INTERVALS STAND ON THIS PAGE UNTIL IT IS MADE. Nothing is unpublished and no reader is left with only the narrower one.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.what_this_means_for_this_pool: THE PUBLISHED INTERVAL EXCLUDES 1 AND THE HOUSE-RULE INTERVAL CROSSES IT. A SIGNIFICANCE VERDICT TURNS ON THE INTERVAL METHOD ALONE. A reader shown only the published interval has been told something firmer than the evidence supports; a reader shown only the wider one loses that the contributing trials agree. BOTH ARE HERE.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.read_the_width_with_care: AT k=2 HARTUNG-KNAPP USES t ON ONE DEGREE OF FREEDOM -- 12.7062 against the normal 1.9600 -- and the interval is enormously wider. That width is a property of the method at very few studies, not a measurement of this evidence. It is recorded so a reader can see it; it is NOT presented as the better interval.

POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_only_one_of_these_two_trials_is_an_afr: READ THIS BESIDE THE ESTIMATE. HPTN 084 (NCT03164564) ran in BOTSWANA, ESWATINI, KENYA, MALAWI, SOUTH AFRICA, UGANDA AND ZIMBABWE, in cisgender women. HPTN 083 (NCT02720094) ran in ARGENTINA, BRAZIL, PERU, SOUTH AFRICA, THAILAND, THE UNITED STATES AND VIETNAM, in men who have sex with men and transgender women -- ONE AFRICAN COUNTRY OF SEVEN -- and it carries the larger weight in this pool. A reader taking this page as evidence about African populations is taking half of it from a trial that was mostly not African and not in women.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_the_heterogeneity_has_a_name: I-squared is 68.83% with tau-squared 0.4178. At k = 2 that statistic proves little by itself, BUT IT DOES NOT STAND BY ITSELF: the two estimates are 0.3335 (0.1785 to 0.6230) in one population and 0.1108 (0.0395 to 0.3107) in the other, and the populations differ by sex, by risk route and by region. The spread has a named cause rather than an unexplained one.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.c_a_published_synthesis_reproduces_this_: Wang et al. 2023 (PMID 37498645) report RR 0.21 (0.07 to 0.61), I-squared 70%, on 17 and 75 events. This object reports 0.2081 (0.0715 to 0.6057), I-squared 68.83%, ON THE SAME 17 AND 75 EVENTS. The arithmetic here has an independent external check and it passes -- which is a statement about the computation, not about whether the two trials should have been combined.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.d_a_registered_safety_co_primary_is_not_: Both registrations register grade 2 or higher adverse events as a SECOND PRIMARY OUTCOME. This review carries only the efficacy primary, so this page is not a benefit-and-harm summary.

Note for identity: HPTN 083 registers its arms as 'Arm A' and 'Arm B', BOTH TYPED EXPERIMENTAL, so the comparator identity is NOT established from that design module -- it is established from HPTN 084, which types its TDF/FTC arm ACTIVE_COMPARATOR, and from this object's own recorded contrast.

D5_selection_of_the_reported_result.reason: TWO primary outcomes are registered, but the second is SAFETY -- adverse events -- not a competing measure of efficacy. There is no set of efficacy endpoints to choose between, so the selection concern found on gepotidacin and inclisiran cannot arise here. RECORDED SEPARATELY AND NOT SCORED: this review does not carry the registered safety co-primary at all.

NCT02720094.overall_reason: D1, D4 and D5 LOW on read registrations; D2 and D3 NO_INFORMATION. The unjudgeable domains are adherence and attrition, and in a trial whose whole premise is that an INJECTION is adhered to better than a DAILY PILL, the adherence domain is not a formality -- it is the mechanism of the effect.

risk_of_bias.sources_NOT_read: The trial publications. D2 and D3 are the domains that depend on them, and both are NO_INFORMATION for that reason.

ceiling.statement: A domain that cannot be judged from the sources read is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect. Overall is capped at SOME_CONCERNS wherever a domain is NO_INFORMATION.
ceiling.shape_note: A DICT, NOT A STRING -- paper_projector does ceil.get('statement'), and a bare string collapses the manuscript to a projector-failed banner (registry class 70).

risk_of_bias.analysis_population_NOT_stated: NEITHER REGISTRATION NAMES THE ANALYSIS POPULATION FOR THE POOLED RESULT. Registered enrolment against participants pooled: HPTN 083 4570 v 4561; HPTN 084 3224 v 3224. P48 -- estimand_established certifies MEASUREMENT, not the population the measurement was taken in.
risk_of_bias.registered_co_primary_not_carried: BOTH registrations register TWO primary outcomes and on both the second is SAFETY. This review carries only the efficacy primary. Recorded as scope, not scored as D5 selection, because there is no competing EFFICACY endpoint to have chosen between.
risk_of_bias.ONE_ASSESSOR_ONLY: ASSESSED BY ONE ASSESSOR. Under the standing specification that risk of bias 2 must be complete and done by TWO AIs from different model families, THIS ASSESSMENT IS INCOMPLETE. It is recorded as such rather than presented as finished, and `rob2.assessors` is deliberately NOT written.

grade.approach: GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.

steps.reason: Both results are SOME_CONCERNS. Randomised, quadruple-masked including the outcomes assessor, single unambiguous efficacy primary -- but D2 and D3 are NO_INFORMATION, and the comparator arm here is a DAILY ORAL PILL whose adherence is precisely what the unread domain would describe.

tau-squared 0.4178, Q 3.2077 on 1 df, p = 0.0733, I-squared 68.83%. At k = 2 the statistic is weak evidence on its own, but it does not stand on its own here: THE TWO TRIALS ARE IN DIFFERENT POPULATIONS. 0.3335 (0.1785 to 0.6230) in men who have sex with men and transgender women, and 0.1108 (0.0395 to 0.3107) in cisgender women. A named reason for the spread is stronger than the statistic.

steps.move: LOW to VERY LOW, down 1 level(s)
steps.reason: THE POOL CROSSES BOTH POPULATION AND REGION. HPTN 084 ran in SEVEN African countries in FEMALE participants. HPTN 083 ran in men who have sex with men and transgender women across Argentina, Brazil, Peru, South Africa, Thailand, the United States and Vietnam -- SEVEN COUNTRIES OF WHICH ONE IS AFRICAN -- and it is the larger and more precisely estimated of the two. A single ratio assembled across those two is not a quantity that answers either question cleanly.

steps.move: VERY LOW -- already at the floor, no further downgrade applied
steps.reason: k = 2. The Hartung-Knapp interval is RR 0.2081 (0.0002 to 212.2504) on t = 12.7062 with 1 df, which carries no information at all. The rating cannot fall below VERY LOW, so this domain is recorded as warranting a downgrade the scale cannot express. THE UNADJUSTED INTERVAL, 0.0715 to 0.6057, still excludes no difference by a wide margin.

primary.summary: LOW certainty, and the reason is not the size of the effect -- which is large, consistent in direction, and reproduced exactly by a published synthesis. It is that TWO TRIALS IN TWO DIFFERENT POPULATIONS ACROSS TWO REGIONS have been combined into one ratio, with I-squared 68.83%, and that the adherence domain both trials turn on was not read.
primary.rating_up_not_applied: No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect, a dose-response gradient or opposing plausible confounding applies to observational evidence; these are randomised trials, which start HIGH.

reviews.their_k_basis: TRANSCRIBED FROM THIS RECORD'S OWN STORED SENTENCE, 'twelve trials, of which seven are prevention trials', which states the count as a WORD. No included-study list was read, so this is a COUNT AND NOT AN IDENTIFICATION -- which trials they carry remains unestablished. Written by hand rather than parsed, because a number spelled out is exactly what an automated count misses.

published_comparison.THE_FINDING_OF_THIS_COMPARISON_2026_08_2: THE CLOSEST AGREEMENT WITH A PUBLISHED SYNTHESIS ANYWHERE IN THIS CORPUS. Wang et al., JMIR Public Health and Surveillance 2023, PMID 37498645, report CAB-LA versus TDF/FTC for prevention as RR 0.21 (95% CI 0.07 to 0.61), I-squared 70%, on 17 events of 5,161 against 75 of 5,129. This object reports RR 0.2081 (0.0715 to 0.6057), I-squared 68.83%, on 13 + 4 = 17 events against 39 + 36 = 75. THE EVENT COUNTS ARE THE SAME NUMBERS. THE ONE PLACE THE TWO DIFFER. They pool 5,161 and 5,129 participants; this object pools 3,894 and 3,891 -- about 1,250 more per arm on their side, CONTRIBUTING NO EVENTS. Nothing read explains where those participants come from; the candidates are a wider analysis population on the same two trials, or a further prevention trial with zero infections. WHICH IT IS HAS NOT BEEN ESTABLISHED and no included-study table was opened. Their review states TWELVE trials -- seven of them prevention trials -- against this object's TWO. On the stated count alone that is the largest gap in the corpus. YET THE CONTRAST ITSELF RESTS ON THE SAME SEVENTEEN AND SEVENTY-FIVE EVENTS. A STATED TRIAL COUNT AND THE EVIDENCE CONTRIBUTING TO A PARTICULAR CONTRAST ARE DIFFERENT THINGS, and this topic is the proof. It is why class 82 reports 'ours lower' and 'trials identified' as SEPARATE states, and why the four count-only topics are worded as a difference in stated counts and nothing more. WHAT THE AGREEMENT DOES NOT CERTIFY IS THAT THE POOL IS A GOOD IDEA. The two trials are in DIFFERENT POPULATIONS across DIFFERENT REGIONS and I-squared is 68.83%. A second team reaching the same number from the same events does not make the combination appropriate -- it makes the arithmetic checked. GRADE certainty here is LOW and indirectness is rated down.

model_output.SUPERSEDED_LOCATION_2026_08_21: THIS TOP-LEVEL COPY IS NOT THE ONE ANYTHING READS. The scorer (scripts/p46_queue.py) and the manuscript projector both look for `results.by_outcome.<outcome>.r_output.verbatim`, and this key was invented by the applier that wrote it. While it sat here, p46_queue scored limb 4 ABSENT on this topic -- 'no quoted output and no stated reason' -- and the topic was REPORTED AS 4 OF 4 WHEN IT WAS 3 OF 4. Kept rather than deleted because a net deletion from an SSOT object breaks a standing rule; read the house key.
